title: Natural descent of a strict quotient-stalk isomorphism
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite-dimensional field extension of Q_l, D a finite-field datum with characteristic p and chosen algebraic closure k of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], l distinct from p, and T a scheme with l invertible in every residue field. Use the integral constructible full subcategory of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the good complexes of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], and the quotient towers, Roos maps and prescribed realization arrows of [lem-trf-bounded-quotient-stalk-realization]. Write J_u for its completed point-fibre functor at u:Spec(k) to T. Let e_u be a family of natural isomorphisms from the strict quotient section tower to its quotient stalk tower for every point u of T. Assume that the prescribed realization arrow e_(u,P):J_u(M) to Q Roos(((P_n)_u)_n) is an isomorphism for every constructible M and every good representative P with q:Q(P) isomorphic to M, and is natural for every chain map between representatives of constructible objects, with its compatible derived arrow. Given any two geometric points v,w and any natural isomorphism R of their strict quotient-stalk tower functors, there exists a natural isomorphism r:J_v to J_w on the full integral constructible category such that, for every M,P,q, r_M followed by e_(w,P) equals e_(v,P) followed by Q Roos(R_P). This assertion involves just one fixed R; it assumes and asserts no automorphism action, strict tower normalization, cone projection law, or truncation law.

proof.text: Flat-term K-flat representatives are essentially surjective onto the ambient derived category by the good-complex localization. Choose one representative for each constructible object. It has constructible derived class by definition. Define each component in diagrammatic order as the source realization, then the localized strict Roos isomorphism of R, then the inverse of the target realization. The given realization-isomorphism hypothesis and the functoriality of Roos make this an isomorphism.

proof.text: For a compatible chain map, naturality of R gives a square of tower maps. The strict Roos functor and derived localization preserve this square. Combining it with the two assumed realization naturality equations proves naturality of the conjugated components for that chain map. The whole-cocone functor respects representative homotopies: the homotopy on the two coordinates is (-product(h),product(h)); transition compatibility cancels the mixed terms. Thus the chain calculations also hold in the homotopy category.

proof.text: Represent any derived arrow by a roof in the homotopy category, with a quasi-isomorphism denominator. Resolve the apex by a flat-term K-flat complex and precompose numerator and denominator. The new apex has derived class isomorphic to the source, hence is constructible; completeness, reduction constructibility and the uniform cohomological bound are invariant under isomorphism. Therefore the assumed naturality and realization-isomorphism clauses apply to all three objects of this roof.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers (b), lines 34--52; expansion of the reviewed parent germ reparametrization proof, Stacks sites.tex Tag 05V1 and sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YT.

proof.text: For the denominator, the assumed realization naturality square identifies its localized Roos map with a derived isomorphism, so invert that square. Compose it with the numerator square. This gives naturality for the derived arrow itself, independent of the chosen roof. Apply this argument to the identity of an object and any second good representative to prove the comparison equation for every P and q. The component maps therefore form the required natural isomorphism, and no automorphism action law is part of this assertion.

theorem trfQuotientStalkNaturalDescent
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [∀ x : T, Invertible (l : T.residueField x)]
    (e : ∀ v : Spec (.of D.k) ⟶ T,
      trfQuotientSectionTower l E v ≅ trfQuotientStalkTower l E v)
    (he : ∀ (v : Spec (.of D.k) ⟶ T) (M : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E T)
      (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E T).FullSubcategory)
      (q : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj ≅ M.obj),
      IsIso (trfQuotientStalkRealizationArrow l E D v (e v) M.obj P q))
    (hnat : ∀ (v : Spec (.of D.k) ⟶ T)
      (M M' : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E T))
      (_hM : sfIntegralConstructible l E T M) (_hM' : sfIntegralConstructible l E T M')
      (P P' : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E T).FullSubcategory)
      (q : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj ≅ M) (q' : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P'.obj ≅ M')
      (w : P.obj ⟶ P'.obj) (h : M ⟶ M'),
      DerivedCategory.Q.map w ≫ q'.hom = q.hom ≫ h →
      (trfCompletedPointFibre l E D v).map h ≫
          trfQuotientStalkRealizationArrow l E D v (e v) M' P' q' =
        trfQuotientStalkRealizationArrow l E D v (e v) M P q ≫
          (trfIntegralModuleQ l E).map
            (integralOperationsRoosMap ((trfQuotientStalkTower l E v).map w)))
    (v w : Spec (.of D.k) ⟶ T)
    (R : trfQuotientStalkTower l E v ≅ trfQuotientStalkTower l E w) :
    ∃ r : (sfIntegralConstructible l E T).ι ⋙ trfCompletedPointFibre l E D v ≅
        (sfIntegralConstructible l E T).ι ⋙ trfCompletedPointFibre l E D w,
      ∀ (M : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E T)
        (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E T).FullSubcategory)
        (q : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj ≅ M.obj),
        r.hom.app M ≫ trfQuotientStalkRealizationArrow l E D w (e w) M.obj P q =
          trfQuotientStalkRealizationArrow l E D v (e v) M.obj P q ≫
            (trfIntegralModuleQ l E).map
              (integralOperationsRoosMap (R.hom.app P.obj))
